title: 02. Ingestion & Chunking: Cross-page references
summary: Scenario from the user: A legal or medical document has clauses that reference other sections. Example: "The obligations set forth in Section 4.1 shall survive termination." Section 4.1 may be 30 pages away.
objectives: Step 3 — Optional Sub-Chunking for Better Retrieval
Step 5 — Index Both Parents and Children in ChromaDB

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
**Scenario from the user:** A legal or medical document has clauses that reference other
sections. Example: *"The obligations set forth in Section 4.1 shall survive termination."*
Section 4.1 may be 30 pages away. A naive chunker places the referencing clause in chunk N
and the referenced section in chunk M. When the retriever returns only chunk N, the LLM
hallucinates the contents of Section 4.1.

**This notebook demonstrates:**
1. Generate a synthetic 10-section contract with cross-references.
2. Section-aware chunking via `MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter` (each chunk carries its section path).
3. Build a **reference graph** — for every chunk, what other chunks does it reference?
4. **Parent-child retrieval**: match on small chunks, return the parent section for context.
5. **Reference expansion**: when a chunk is retrieved, also pull the chunks it references.
6. Retrieval test proving both the reference and its target are returned.

**Library focus:** `langchain-text-splitters` + `chromadb` + `sentence-transformers`.

```python
# Install dependencies (uncomment on first run)
# !pip install langchain-text-splitters==0.2.0 chromadb==0.5.0 sentence-transformers==2.7.0
```

```python
import re
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Dict, Any
from collections import defaultdict

from langchain_text_splitters import MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter, RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
import chromadb
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

WORKDIR = Path("/tmp/rag_legal_nb2")
WORKDIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
print(f"Workdir: {WORKDIR}")
```

sections.title: Step 1 — Generate a Synthetic 10-Section Contract
sections.body:
Each section is short but cross-references other sections. The contract mimics the structure
of a real SaaS agreement. References are explicit ("Section 4.1", "Exhibit A") so we can
detect them with regex.

```python
CONTRACT_MD = """# Master Services Agreement

## 1. Definitions

"**Affiliate**" means any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party.
"**Confidential Information**" has the meaning given in Section 5.
"**Services**" means the SaaS services described in Exhibit A.
"**Effective Date**" means the date set forth in the Order Form referenced in Section 3.

## 2. Grant of License

Subject to the terms of this Agreement and Section 4, the Provider grants the Customer a
non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use the Services for the term specified in Section 8.
The license is contingent on timely payment as set forth in Section 4.2.

## 3. Order Form

The Customer shall submit an Order Form referencing the Effective Date and the Services
selected from Exhibit A. Each Order Form constitutes a separate order under this Agreement.

## 4. Fees and Payment

### 4.1 Fees

Fees for the Services are set forth in Exhibit A. All fees are due in USD within thirty (30)
days of the invoice date, except as provided in Section 4.2.

### 4.2 Late Payment

Any payment not received within forty-five (45) days of the invoice date shall accrue interest
at 1.5% per month. The Provider may suspend access to the Services after sixty (60) days of
non-payment, subject to the notice requirements in Section 7.

## 5. Confidentiality

Each party shall protect Confidential Information with the same degree of care it uses for its
own confidential information, but no less than reasonable care. The obligations in this Section 5
shall survive termination of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years, as provided in
Section 8.3.

## 6. Intellectual Property

The Provider retains all right, title, and interest in the Services, including all intellectual
property rights therein. Customer feedback provided under Section 2 may be used by the Provider
to improve the Services.

## 7. Termination

Either party may terminate this Agreement for material breach upon thirty (30) days written
notice, except that the Provider may terminate immediately for non-payment as provided in
Section 4.2. Upon termination, the surviving obligations set forth in Section 5 and Section 8.3
shall continue in effect.

## 8. Miscellaneous

### 8.1 Governing Law

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to its
conflict-of-laws provisions.

### 8.2 Assignment

The Customer may not assign this Agreement without the Provider's prior written consent. Any
attempted assignment in violation of this Section 8.2 is void.

### 8.3 Survival

The obligations set forth in Section 1 (Definitions), Section 5 (Confidentiality), and
Section 6 (Intellectual Property) shall survive termination of this Agreement.

## Exhibit A. Services Description

The Services include: (i) the SaaS platform described in the documentation, (ii) standard
support during business hours, and (iii) access to the API. Premium support is available for
an additional fee as set forth in the Order Form referenced in Section 3.
"""

contract_path = WORKDIR / "contract.md"
contract_path.write_text(CONTRACT_MD)
print(f"Contract length: {len(CONTRACT_MD)} chars, {CONTRACT_MD.count(chr(10))} lines")
print(f"Cross-references found:")
refs = re.findall(r"(?:Section|Exhibit)\s+[\dIVX.]+[A-Z]?", CONTRACT_MD)
print(f"  {len(refs)} total references: {refs[:10]} ...")
```

sections.title: Step 2 — Section-Aware Chunking
sections.body:
`MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter` splits on `#`, `##`, `###` headers. Each resulting chunk's
`.metadata` carries the full section path, e.g. `{"Header 1": "4", "Header 2": "4.2"}`.

We then combine the section path into a single string like `"4 > 4.2"` for easy storage.

```python
headers_to_split_on = [
    ("#", "Header 1"),
    ("##", "Header 2"),
    ("###", "Header 3"),
]
md_splitter = MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter(headers_to_split_on)
md_chunks = md_splitter.split_text(CONTRACT_MD)

# Convert to a clean list of dicts
parsed_chunks: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
for i, c in enumerate(md_chunks):
    section_path = " > ".join(
        v for v in [c.metadata.get("Header 1"), c.metadata.get("Header 2"), c.metadata.get("Header 3")]
        if v
    )
    parsed_chunks.append({
        "id": f"chunk_{i}",
        "text": c.page_content.strip(),
        "section_path": section_path,
        "section_number": c.metadata.get("Header 2") or c.metadata.get("Header 1") or "",
        "exhibit": c.metadata.get("Header 1") if c.metadata.get("Header 1", "").startswith("Exhibit") else None,
    })

print(f"Number of section-aware chunks: {len(parsed_chunks)}")
for c in parsed_chunks:
    print(f"  {c['id']}  section='{c['section_path']}'  chars={len(c['text'])}")
```

sections.title: Step 3 — Optional Sub-Chunking for Better Retrieval
sections.body:
Section-aware chunks can be long. For precise embedding match, sub-chunk each section with a
recursive character splitter, but tag every sub-chunk with its parent section id. We then
embed the small sub-chunks but retrieve the parent section — this is the **parent-child**
retrieval pattern.

```python
rc_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=400, chunk_overlap=50)
child_chunks: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
for parent in parsed_chunks:
    sub_texts = rc_splitter.split_text(parent["text"])
    if not sub_texts:
        sub_texts = [parent["text"]]
    for j, st in enumerate(sub_texts):
        child_chunks.append({
            "id": f"{parent['id']}_{j}",
            "parent_id": parent["id"],
            "text": st,
            "section_path": parent["section_path"],
            "section_number": parent["section_number"],
        })

print(f"Parent chunks: {len(parsed_chunks)}")
print(f"Child chunks:  {len(child_chunks)}")
```

sections.title: Step 4 — Build the Reference Graph
sections.body:
For every child chunk, scan its text for references like `Section 4.1` or `Exhibit A`.
Resolve each reference to the target parent chunk's id using the section_path index.

```python
SECTION_REF = re.compile(r"Section\s+([\d.]+)")
EXHIBIT_REF = re.compile(r"Exhibit\s+([A-Z])")

# Build section-number -> parent_id index
section_index: Dict[str, str] = {}
exhibit_index: Dict[str, str] = {}
for p in parsed_chunks:
    if p["section_number"]:
        section_index[p["section_number"]] = p["id"]
    if p["exhibit"]:
        # extract letter e.g. "Exhibit A" -> "A"
        m = re.match(r"Exhibit\s+([A-Z])", p["exhibit"])
        if m:
            exhibit_index[m.group(1)] = p["id"]

print("Section index:", section_index)
print("Exhibit index:", exhibit_index)
print()

# Build reference graph on parent chunks
reference_graph: Dict[str, List[str]] = defaultdict(list)
for p in parsed_chunks:
    sec_refs = SECTION_REF.findall(p["text"])
    ex_refs = EXHIBIT_REF.findall(p["text"])
    targets = [section_index[r] for r in sec_refs if r in section_index]
    targets += [exhibit_index[r] for r in ex_refs if r in exhibit_index]
    # De-duplicate, exclude self
    targets = list({t for t in targets if t != p["id"]})
    reference_graph[p["id"]] = targets
    if targets:
        print(f"  {p['id']} ({p['section_path']}) -> references {targets}")

# Save the graph
(WORKDIR / "reference_graph.json").write_text(json.dumps(reference_graph, indent=2))
```

sections.title: Step 5 — Index Both Parents and Children in ChromaDB
sections.body:
- `parent_sections` collection: large chunks returned to the LLM at generation time.
- `child_chunks` collection: small chunks used for precise embedding match.

We also store `references` (the reference graph) in metadata so we can expand at retrieval.

```python
embedder = SentenceTransformer("BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5")

client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=str(WORKDIR / "chroma_db"))
for name in ["parent_sections", "child_chunks"]:
    try: client.delete_collection(name)
    except: pass

parent_coll = client.create_collection("parent_sections", metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"})
child_coll = client.create_collection("child_chunks", metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"})

# Index parents
parent_texts = [p["text"] for p in parsed_chunks]
parent_vecs = embedder.encode(parent_texts, normalize_embeddings=True).tolist()
parent_coll.add(
    ids=[p["id"] for p in parsed_chunks],
    documents=parent_texts,
    embeddings=parent_vecs,
    metadatas=[{
        "section_path": p["section_path"],
        "section_number": p["section_number"],
        "references": json.dumps(reference_graph[p["id"]]),
    } for p in parsed_chunks],
)

# Index children
child_texts = [c["text"] for c in child_chunks]
child_vecs = embedder.encode(child_texts, normalize_embeddings=True).tolist()
child_coll.add(
    ids=[c["id"] for c in child_chunks],
    documents=child_texts,
    embeddings=child_vecs,
    metadatas=[{
        "parent_id": c["parent_id"],
        "section_path": c["section_path"],
    } for c in child_chunks],
)

print(f"Indexed {len(parsed_chunks)} parent sections and {len(child_chunks)} child chunks.")
```

sections.title: Step 6 — Retrieval with Reference Expansion
sections.body:
The retrieval function:
1. Embeds the query, matches against `child_chunks` (top 3).
2. Collects the unique `parent_id`s of those children.
3. **Reference expansion**: for each parent, look up its `references` and pull those parents too.
4. Returns the union — both the matching section AND the sections it references.

```python
def retrieve_with_references(query: str, n_children: int = 3) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    qv = embedder.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True).tolist()
    child_res = child_coll.query(query_embeddings=qv, n_results=n_children)

    matched_parent_ids = []
    seen = set()
    for meta in child_res["metadatas"][0]:
        pid = meta["parent_id"]
        if pid not in seen:
            matched_parent_ids.append(pid)
            seen.add(pid)

    # Reference expansion: pull parents referenced by matched parents
    expanded_ids = list(matched_parent_ids)
    for pid in matched_parent_ids:
        # Fetch this parent's references
        parent_data = parent_coll.get(ids=[pid])
        if parent_data["metadatas"]:
            refs = json.loads(parent_data["metadatas"][0].get("references", "[]"))
            for r in refs:
                if r not in seen:
                    expanded_ids.append(r)
                    seen.add(r)

    # Fetch the full parent documents
    final = parent_coll.get(ids=expanded_ids)
    return {
        "query": query,
        "matched_parents": matched_parent_ids,
        "expanded_parents": expanded_ids,
        "documents": final["documents"],
        "metadatas": final["metadatas"],
    }
```

```python
test_queries = [
    "What happens if I breach confidentiality?",
    "When can the provider suspend access to the services?",
    "What survives termination of the agreement?",
    "What is the governing law?",
]

for q in test_queries:
    print(f"\n=== Query: {q}")
    result = retrieve_with_references(q, n_children=3)
    print(f"  Matched parents:   {result['matched_parents']}")
    print(f"  Expanded parents:  {result['expanded_parents']}")
    for i, (doc, meta) in enumerate(zip(result["documents"], result["metadatas"])):
        print(f"  [{i}] section={meta['section_path']}")
        print(f"      preview: {doc[:160]!r}")
```

### Expected outcome

For the query *"What happens if I breach confidentiality?"*:
- The matched parent should be Section 5 (Confidentiality) — it mentions the breach.
- The expanded parents should include Section 8.3 (Survival) — because Section 5 references it
  for the survival period — and Section 1 (Definitions) — because "Confidential Information"
  is defined there.

For *"When can the provider suspend access?"*:
- Matched parent: Section 4.2 (Late Payment) — it mentions suspension.
- Expanded: Section 7 (Termination) — because Section 4.2 references the notice requirements
  in Section 7.

Without reference expansion, the retriever would return only the matched parent and the LLM
would have to guess what Section 8.3 or Section 7 says. With expansion, both sections are
returned and the LLM can answer accurately.

sections.title: Summary
sections.body:
| Step | What we did | Why |
|------|-------------|-----|
| 1 | Generated a 10-section contract with explicit cross-references | Reproducible test corpus |
| 2 | Section-aware chunking with `MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter` | Each chunk carries its section path |
| 3 | Sub-chunked for precise embedding match | Small chunks match better |
| 4 | Built reference graph by regex-scanning for `Section X` / `Exhibit Y` | Know what each chunk points to |
| 5 | Indexed parents + children in two Chroma collections | Parent-child retrieval pattern |
| 6 | Retrieval with reference expansion | Both reference and target are returned |

**Key takeaway:** For documents with cross-page references, chunking alone is not enough.
You need a **reference graph** and **expansion at retrieval time** so that the LLM gets both
the matching chunk AND the chunks it points to. This pattern generalizes to medical records
(patient ID references), research papers (citation references), and any corpus with
explicit cross-references.
